metrics.samples: 31 positive calibrated batch-averaged per-operation values; p95 is a percentile of batch means, not individual-call tail latency
metrics.rust_allocation: separate System allocation/reallocation requests and requested Layout byte sums
metrics.go_allocation: testing.AllocsPerRun and separate average MemStats.TotalAlloc; Go accounting may be fractional/rounded; neither metric is RSS
metrics.timing: Normal Go GC during timing; both probes calibrate to three confirmations at 20 ms. Adaptive iteration counts differ; historical fixed-count comparator is unchanged.

findings: All six complete frame outputs, styles, first-return values and semantics match in both balanced pairs for both sources.
Default percentage labels remove two requested heap operations and 12 requested bytes per call. All six borrowed-cell controls request zero allocations in both final runs.
Full frame construction remains six requested allocations per measured case; no zero-allocation View/Surface claim.
Finite current frame medians are about 4.6–22.9% of the reference. Some p95 observations worsen versus the baseline; retain both cohorts without a blanket timing improvement claim.
limits: One macOS arm64 host, no frequency/affinity control, background system work uncontrolled. Owned build/test/Miri/LLVM/download work finished before each measurement.
Complete 0.625-fraction frames at six fixed configurations only; constructors, dynamic lifecycle, scheduling/errors/other widths/percentages and high-depth/alpha inputs remain pending.
No current-source cross-platform timing comparison, whole-framework optimization, module parity, global maximum speed or quality score promotion.
